requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The change generates a formatter in the consuming assembly for a type from a referenced assembly, which L11 says the compiler deliberately does not do (TypeCollector skips metadata-only types). This is not a defect: the new path bypasses TypeCollector via an explicit opt-in attribute, so the L11 behavior for implicit types is unchanged.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: Contractless mode serializes types lacking [MessagePackObject] and [Key]. L3 and L8 record that requiring MessagePackObject is intentional for explicitness. The new feature is opt-in per formatter and the requirement explicitly asks for contractless-by-default here, so it is consistent.

findings.claim: Public field selection is inverted. `IsPublicReadWrite` keeps only `readonly` fields (`field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst`). As a result, ordinary public mutable fields of T are silently left out of the contractless formatter, which loses data on round-trip. Public `readonly` fields are included instead, so the generated code tries to assign to them on deserialize. This breaks the criterion 'contractless behaviour over public members', and it contradicts the attribute docs and README ('every public, read-write instance property and field').

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterContractlessFidelityTests.PublicMutableField_IsSerializedInContractlessMode. ProjectA.MyObject has `public string FieldMember;`. On head the generated formatter source does not contain FieldMember, so the test fails.

findings.claim: Attributes on T are never honoured. When no SurrogateType is set, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type). It ignores [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] and [DataContract]/[DataMember] on T, so members excluded by T's own contract are still serialized under name keys. This misses the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured'. It also misses the maintainer rule that contractless applies only when T has no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject].

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterContractlessFidelityTests.DataContractAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured and MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured. On head the generated formatter contains the non-DataMember / [IgnoreMember] member name, so both tests fail.

findings.claim: IsPublicReadWrite has its field check inverted: `field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst` should be `!field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst`. In contractless mode a plain public mutable field (`public int MutableField;`) is silently left out of serialization, which breaks the requirement that public members are serialized. A `public readonly` field is included and marked writable, so the generated Deserialize assigns to a readonly field and the formatter fails to compile (CS0191). Surrogate mode uses the same predicate, so a surrogate keyed on a mutable field gets MsgPack022, while one keyed on a readonly field produces uncompilable code.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterReceiptsTests.Contractless_PublicMutableField_IsSerialized and Contractless_ReadOnlyField_DoesNotBreakGeneratedFormatter. ProjectA.Data has `public int MutableField; public readonly int ReadOnlyField;` in a referenced assembly. On head the first test fails because the generated formatter never mentions MutableField. The second fails because the generated tree has CS0191 errors.

hunches.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. When no surrogate is given, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers and never reads [MessagePackObject], [Key] or [IgnoreMember] on T. A referenced type with `[MessagePackObject] class Data { [Key(0)] int Value; [IgnoreMember] int Hidden; }` therefore gets a string-keyed formatter that serializes Hidden and ignores the declared int keys. This is wire-incompatible with the dynamic resolver and with the defining assembly's own contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterReceiptsTests.AttributedType_IgnoreMember_IsHonoured. The referenced ProjectA.Data has [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] Value and [IgnoreMember] Hidden. On head the generated DataFormatter source contains 'Hidden'.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats public fields as serializable only if they are readonly (field.IsReadOnly). Public mutable fields are skipped and readonly fields are included. Readonly fields cannot be assigned in the generated deserializer, so it either fails to compile or the fields are silently dropped. The doc comment says read-write members are serialized.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class IMessagePackFormatter<T> where T has `public int F;` and `public readonly int R;`. Regenerate and check that F is emitted and R is not, and that the output compiles.

hunches.claim: The new generated-formatter diagnostics (MsgPack019-022) are added to SupportedDiagnostics, but diagnostics are only reported from a source-generator output. MsgPack019-022 are not added to AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md, which can trigger RS2000 in builds. Also, the partial check only inspects the syntax on one declaration.

receipt_plan.detail: Build MessagePack.SourceGenerator with warnings-as-errors and check for RS2000 on MsgPack019-022 missing from AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md.

hunches.claim: In surrogate mode with string keys, the member's IntKey is set to members.Count, which follows declaration order. Reordering declarations on the surrogate changes the generated member order. For int keys, sparse keys are passed straight through, and the string-key and int-key templates may not cope with gaps.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter with a surrogate that has int keys [Key(0)] and [Key(2)]. Check that the output compiles and that serialization round-trips with the expected array length.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats any public field as eligible only if it is readonly (field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst). That inverts the check: writable public fields are excluded and readonly fields are included. The generated deserializer will then assign to readonly fields, which fails to compile or breaks the generated code. Mutable fields are silently omitted from the wire contract, so the formatter does not serialize or populate them.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator snapshot test with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] over a referenced-assembly type with a public mutable field and a public readonly field. Assert the mutable field is serialized and the readonly field is not. It currently fails.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats a public field as writable only if field.IsReadOnly is true. This is inverted: it accepts readonly fields and rejects normal mutable public fields. Mutable public fields are skipped, and readonly fields would generate uncompilable assignments. This contradicts the README claim that public read-write fields are serialized.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external class with `public int F;` and a `public readonly int R;`, generate a contractless formatter, and round-trip. F is dropped, and R produces a CS0191 compile error.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats a public field as eligible only when field.IsReadOnly is true, so the condition is inverted. Writable public fields are skipped and readonly fields are included, which would break deserialization. No test uses a public field on any external type, so nothing would notice.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:268 negate-condition: field.IsReadOnly -> !field.IsReadOnly; expected to survive because ExternalPerson, ExternalPoint and ExternalWidget declare only properties, so no test exercises the field branch. A test with a public mutable field on an external type would fail on head.

hunches.claim: The test of 'only public members' never checks that non-public members are skipped. ExternalPerson has no private/internal/protected members and no private-setter property. Mutating the accessibility checks in IsPublicReadWrite (for example, dropping the SetMethod public check) would only be caught by the read-only Doubled property.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:263 remove-guard: drop `property.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public` and the GetMethod accessibility check; expected to survive because no external type has a non-public or private-set member.

hunches.claim: The surrogate key-kind and key-uniqueness paths are weakly covered. SurrogateKeysMustNotMixStringAndInt expects MsgPack005 only from the analyzer path, but the Collect call that reports it is invoked with the diagnostic list in the generator. The duplicate-key check (KeysMustBeUnique) has no test, and neither does the string-key surrogate path (the `(string)key` branch). The ExecutionTests surrogate uses only int keys, so the string-key surrogate branch has no round-trip test.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:176 remove-guard: delete the `if (!claimedKeys.Add(key))` block; expected to survive because no test has duplicate surrogate keys. Also swap `CreateMember(target, intKey: members.Count, stringKey: (string)key)` args; expected to survive because there is no string-key surrogate test.

hunches.claim: No test covers the guard that excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from the hand-written formatter registration in GeneratorUtilities. Removing it could duplicate the registration. GeneratedFormattersAreRegisteredInGeneratedResolver would likely pass either way if the duplicate resolves to the same formatter, and there is no snapshot test.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: delete `&& !symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttributeName...)`; expected to survive or at most yield a duplicate registration the tests never inspect.

hunches.claim: Missing negative cases: there are no tests for MsgPack021 on a generic or inaccessible type, for a class without a parameterless constructor (NoDeserializingConstructor), or for the surrogate member being a read-only or non-public member of T. There are also no generator snapshot tests (regeneration) for the new formatter output, so the template change (`partial class`) is verified only through the ExecutionTests.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:68 remove-guard: delete the `!compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter)` and `isClass && !...InstanceConstructors.Any` checks; expected to survive because only the abstract-type case is tested for MsgPack021 and no test lacks a default constructor.

hunches.claim: The int-key contractless/surrogate path is checked loosely. SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership asserts only the array length (8), not that Id sits at index 3 and Name at index 7, so swapped keys would survive. Also ContractlessClassUsesStringKeys only checks the header byte and substrings in the JSON, not key order (OrderBy ordinal).

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:179 swap: CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey, ...) -> intKey: members.Count; expected to survive only partly: the length would change to 2, so this would be caught, but a swap of two int keys would round-trip fine and survive.

hunches.claim: Contractless members are always built with constructorParameters empty and require a parameterless constructor, but the generator's Collect call passes reportDiagnostic: null. A rejected formatter is silently dropped from the model, and diagnostics come from a separate pipeline. The MessagePackSecurity UntrustedData and depth-limit handling in the shared templates still applies, but it is bypassed if a formatter is silently skipped. This is not a clear defect on its own.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect and MessagePackGenerator.cs:70 and the diagnostics pipeline; confirm each rejection path reports a diagnostic exactly once.

hunches.claim: The new MsgPack019-022 diagnostics are added to the analyzer release notes and docs, but the diagnostics are reported only from the generator via RegisterSourceOutput. The analyzer's Initialize registers no actions for them, so they come from the generator, not the analyzer. Also, MessageFormat arguments for the reused NoDeserializingConstructor, MemberNeedsKey and DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys descriptors may not match their format strings. NoDeserializingConstructor is passed only a location, with no message args.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the argument counts passed to Diagnostic.Create for NoDeserializingConstructor, MemberNeedsKey and KeysMustBeUnique with the messageFormat placeholders in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change implements both contractless mode and the surrogate-type design (SurrogateType property). It adds the new GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute to MessagePack.Annotations, requires integer or string keys on the surrogate, and matches members by name and type.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Contractless-only: the attribute has no SurrogateType, so the generator uses the type's own MessagePack attributes (DataContract, Key, etc.) if present and otherwise contractless. This drops the surrogate path and the MsgPack022 diagnostic, and instead honours existing attributes on T.
